records.content: Bandeng is the milkfish Chanos chanos (Fabricius, 1775), the only species in family Chanidae (order Gonorynchiformes); a marine, freshwater and brackish benthopelagic, amphidromous species of the Indo-West Pacific.
records.source_quote: Teleostei (teleosts) > Gonorynchiformes (Milkfishes) > Chanidae (Milkfish) ... Marine; freshwater; brackish; benthopelagic; amphidromous

records.content: Milkfish have an elongate, somewhat compressed body with a small toothless mouth, falcate pectoral fins and a large deeply forked caudal fin; olive green dorsally with silvery flanks; adults reach 180 cm SL and 14 kg.
records.source_quote: body elongate and somewhat compressed; mouth small and toothless ... pectoral fins falcate; caudal fin large and deeply forked ... Colour of the body olive green dorsally; flanks silvery; unpaired fins with dark margins ... Max length: 180 cm SL ... max. published weight: 14.0 kg

records.content: Bandeng presto (pressurized milkfish) is a well-known product of Pati Regency, one of the largest milkfish producers in Central Java Province; the article characterises the bandeng presto processing chain at small-and-medium-enterprise scale.
records.source_quote: Pati Regency is one of the largest milkfish producers in Central Java Province with one well known product is pressurized milkfish.

records.content: Milkfish is highly commercial in both capture fisheries and aquaculture; larvae are collected from rivers and grown in culture ponds into juveniles marketed fresh, smoked, canned or frozen, and brood stock can be raised and spawned in captivity.
records.source_quote: Fisheries: highly commercial; aquaculture: commercial ... Larvae are collected from rivers and are grown in culture ponds into juveniles which are marketed fresh, smoked, canned or frozen. Brood stocks can be raised and spawned in captivity to produce larvae in the hatchery

records.content: Senangin is the fourfinger threadfin Eleutheronema tetradactylum (Shaw, 1804), family Polynemidae (Threadfins), distinguished by four free pectoral filaments; an Indo-Pacific marine, freshwater and brackish pelagic-neritic species.
records.source_quote: Teleostei (teleosts) > Carangaria/misc (Various families in series Carangaria) > Polynemidae (Threadfins) ... pectoral filaments 4 ... Marine; freshwater; brackish; pelagic-neritic; amphidromous

records.content: Fourfinger threadfin grow to 200 cm TL and 145 kg (common length 50 cm TL); pectoral fin membranes are vivid yellow in life (dusky yellow in large specimens) and pectoral filaments are white; the species is a protandrous hermaphrodite.
records.source_quote: Max length: 200 cm TL ... common length: 50.0 cm TL ... max. published weight: 145.0 kg ... pectoral fin membranes vivid yellow in life, except in large specimens > ca 35 cm SL which is dusky yellow; pectoral filaments white ... Protandrous hermaphrodites.

records.content: Fourfinger threadfin is a highly commercial food fish with commercial aquaculture; adults occur mainly over shallow muddy bottoms in coastal waters and enter rivers; marketed fresh, frozen, and dried or salted.
records.source_quote: Adults occur mainly over shallow muddy bottoms in coastal waters. Also enter rivers ... Marketed fresh, frozen, and dried or salted. ... Fisheries: highly commercial; aquaculture: commercial

records.content: Gulamah is the leaftail croaker Johnius trachycephalus (Bleeker, 1851), a small sciaenid (drums or croakers) of the Indo-Pacific (Thailand, Sumatra, Borneo) reaching 13 cm SL; it inhabits shallow coastal waters, estuaries and rivers and is a food fish.
records.source_quote: Teleostei (teleosts) > Eupercaria/misc (Various families in series Eupercaria) > Sciaenidae (Drums or croakers) ... Max length: 13.0 cm SL ... Inhabits shallow coastal waters, estuaries and rivers (Ref. 9772). A food fish.

records.content: Gulamah (Johnius trachycephalus) is processed into salted fish; the feasibility of salted gulamah fish processing in Perlis Village, Langkat Regency (medium- and micro-scale businesses) was analysed.
records.source_quote: This study aimed to determine the feasibility of processing salted gulamah fish in Perlis Village, Langkat Regency.

records.content: Gelama bunga is the yellow drum Nibea albiflora (Richardson, 1846), family Sciaenidae (drums or croakers), a temperate benthopelagic species of the Northwest Pacific (southern Japan and East China Sea) reaching 43.5 cm SL and 1.5 kg.
records.source_quote: Teleostei (teleosts) > Eupercaria/misc (Various families in series Eupercaria) > Sciaenidae (Drums or croakers) ... Max length: 43.5 cm SL ... max. published weight: 1.5 kg ... Northwest Pacific: southern Japan and East China Sea.

records.content: Yellow drum is a commercially fished species found near shore on mud to sandy-mud bottoms in semi-enclosed sea areas, and is also used in Chinese medicine.
records.source_quote: Found near shore, including semi-enclosed sea areas, in mud to sandy mud bottom ... Used in Chinese medicine ... Fisheries: commercial

records.content: Mujair is the Mozambique tilapia Oreochromis mossambicus (Peters, 1852), family Cichlidae (subfamily Pseudocrenilabrinae); a highly euryhaline freshwater/brackish benthopelagic maternal mouthbrooder, widely introduced for aquaculture and often outcompeting local species where it escapes to the wild.
records.source_quote: Teleostei (teleosts) > Cichliformes (Cichlids, convict blennies) > Cichlidae (Cichlids) > Pseudocrenilabrinae ... Highly euryhaline ... maternal mouthbrooder ... Widely introduced for aquaculture, but escaped and established itself in the wild in many countries, often outcompeting local species

records.content: Mozambique tilapia has excellent palatability with a small head, large dress-out weight and fillets without small bones.
records.source_quote: Excellent palatability (Ref. 6465), with small head and large dress-out weight (Ref. 61), and filets without small bones (Ref. 57960).

records.content: Mozambique tilapia (Oreochromis mossambicus) is processed into fish mince and burger; their quality was evaluated during frozen storage at -18C up to 75 days.
records.source_quote: Quality of Tilapia fish mince and burger were determined during frozen storage condition (-18C) up to 75th days.

records.content: Nila is the Nile tilapia Oreochromis niloticus (Linnaeus, 1758) [Cichlidae]; globally the most important tilapia species in fish farming, and the predominant cultured species among tilapias.
records.source_quote: Oreochromis niloticus (Linnaeus, 1758) [Cichlidae] ... Several species of tilapia are cultured commercially, but Nile tilapia is the predominant cultured species worldwide.

records.content: Nile tilapia is a large deep-bodied tilapia with a relatively small head; its most distinguishing characteristic is regular vertical stripes throughout the depth of the caudal fin at all life stages; reaches 60 cm SL and 4.3 kg.
records.source_quote: A large deep-bodied tilapia, with a relatively small head ... Most distinguishing characteristic is the presence, at all life stages, of regular vertical stripes throughout depth of caudal fin ... Max length: 60.0 cm SL ... max. published weight: 4.3 kg

records.content: Tilapia is the second most important group of farmed fish after carps and the most widely grown of any farmed fish; global tilapia production was projected to increase from 1.5 million tonnes in 2003 to 2.5 million tonnes by 2010, with a sales value above USD 5 billion, most of it attributed to Nile tilapia.
records.source_quote: Tilapia (including all species) is the second most important group of farmed fish after carps, and the most widely grown of any farmed fish ... global production of all species of tilapia is projected to increase from 1.5 million tonnes in 2003 to 2.5 million tonnes by 2010, with a sales value of more than USD 5 billion. Most of this enhanced production is expected to be attributed to Nile tilapia.

records.content: Nile tilapia fillets are described as an ideal menu addition due to their reasonable price, year-round supply, mild, delicious flavour and flexibility in preparation; virtually all casual dining restaurant chains in the USA feature tilapia.
records.source_quote: which are an ideal menu addition due to their reasonable price, year-round supply, mild, delicious flavour and flexibility in preparation. Virtually all casual dining restaurant chains in the USA feature tilapia

records.content: Kembung corresponds to the island mackerel Rastrelliger faughni Matsui, 1967, family Scombridae (mackerels, tunas, bonitos), an epipelagic neritic species of the Indo-West Pacific; recognised by a black blotch behind the pectoral fin base and a yellowish silver belly.
records.source_quote: Teleostei (teleosts) > Scombriformes (Mackerels) > Scombridae (Mackerels, tunas, bonitos) > Scombrinae ... A black blotch behind pectoral fin base. The belly is yellowish silver

records.content: Island mackerel reach 24 cm FL and 750 g, with the head longer than the body depth, 2 to 6 large spots at the base of the first dorsal fin, and a swim bladder present; they form schools of equally sized individuals in waters where surface temperature does not fall below 17C.
records.source_quote: Head longer than body depth. ... Swim bladder present. ... 2 to 6 large spots are at the base of the first dorsal fin ... Max length: 24.0 cm FL ... max. published weight: 750.00 g ... Forms schools of equally sized individuals.

records.content: The value chain of island mackerel (Rastrelliger faughni) in selected coastal municipalities around the Lagonoy Gulf, Philippines was analysed to identify bottlenecks and areas for improvement.
records.source_quote: Analyzing the value chain of island mackerel (Rastrelliger faughni) in the Lagonoy Gulf helps to identify bottlenecks and areas for improvement.

records.content: Kuniran is the goldband goatfish Upeneus moluccensis (Bleeker, 1855), family Mullidae (goatfishes), distinguished by a mid-lateral yellow or gold stripe from the eye to the upper caudal-fin base, white barbels and red caudal-fin bars.
records.source_quote: Teleostei (teleosts) > Mulliformes (Goatfishes) > Mullidae (Goatfishes) ... one mid-lateral body stripe yellow or gold from eye to upper caudal-fin base ... white barbels; silvery-rose body

records.content: Goldband goatfish reach 22.5 cm TL (common length 18 cm TL); they form large schools in coastal waters with a muddy substrate and usually swim fast with short stops to feed.
records.source_quote: Found in coastal waters with a muddy substrate. Forms large schools ... Usually fast swimming with short stops to feed ... Max length: 22.5 cm TL ... common length: 18.0 cm TL

records.content: Goldband goatfish is a commercial food fish sold fresh in markets; it is also utilized for fish meal and valued for its roe.
records.source_quote: Sold fresh in markets. Utilized for fish meal. Valued also for its roe ... Fisheries: commercial

records.content: The sensory acceptability limit of goldband goatfish (Upeneus moluccensis) stored in ice is 8 days (11 days for red mullet), determined through sensory, microbiological and chemical freshness assessment.
records.source_quote: The sensory acceptability limit was 8 days for goldband goatfish (Upeneus moluccensis) and 11 days for red mullet (Mullus barbatus) stored in ice.

records.content: The 'tuna' label is pinned at genus level to Thunnus (family Scombridae), which the FAO Scombrids of the World catalogue treats as seven species: T. alalunga, T. albacares, T. atlanticus, T. maccoyii, T. obesus, T. thynnus and T. tonggol.
records.source_quote: Thunnus: Thunnus alalunga, Thunnus albacares, Thunnus atlanticus, Thunnus maccoyii, Thunnus obesus, Thunnus thynnus, Thunnus tonggol

records.content: The Thunnus chapter of the FAO Scombrids catalogue (AC478E11.pdf) carries the illustrated key to genera and species of Scombridae and the per-species accounts of all seven Thunnus species.
records.source_quote: 2.1 Illustrated Key to Genera and Species of Scombridae ... Thunnus ... Thunnus alalunga, Thunnus albacares, Thunnus atlanticus, Thunnus maccoyii, Thunnus obesus, Thunnus thynnus, Thunnus tonggol

records.content: The FAO Scombrids catalogue is the reference inventory for tuna and mackerel fisheries: it covers all 49 known scombrid species with wide-ranging information on habitat, biology and fisheries.
records.source_quote: The present volume covers all 49 species of scombrids known so far ... wide-ranging information on habitat, biology, and fisheries

records.content: 'Tenggiri' (Bahasa Indonesia and Malay, Indonesia and Malaysia) is a vernacular name shared by five species: Sarda orientalis, Scomberomorus commerson, Scomberomorus guttatus, Scomberomorus koreanus and Scomberomorus lineolatus; the label is therefore ambiguous without a species assignment.
records.source_quote: List of Common Names for 'Tenggiri' [n=7] ... Species: Sarda orientalis, Scomberomorus commerson, Scomberomorus guttatus, Scomberomorus koreanus, Scomberomorus lineolatus

records.content: Scomberomorus commerson (Lacepede, 1800), the narrow-barred Spanish mackerel, is one candidate species for 'tenggiri': a large pelagic scombrid of the Indo-West Pacific reaching 240 cm FL, with iridescent blue-grey back and numerous thin wavy vertical bands.
records.source_quote: Scomberomorus commerson (Lacepede, 1800) ... Narrow-barred Spanish mackerel ... Max length: 240 cm FL ... Colour of back iridescent blue-grey, sides silver with bluish reflections, marked with numerous thin, wavy vertical bands

records.content: Scomberomorus guttatus (Bloch & Schneider, 1801), the Indo-Pacific king mackerel, is another candidate species for 'tenggiri', reaching 81.5 cm FL and 4 kg; sides silvery white with several rows of round dark brownish spots along the lateral line.
records.source_quote: Scomberomorus guttatus (Bloch & Schneider, 1801) ... Indo-Pacific king mackerel ... Sides silvery white with several rows of round dark brownish spots scattered in about three irregular rows along the lateral line ... Max length: 81.5 cm FL ... max. published weight: 4.0 kg

records.content: S. commerson is marketed mainly fresh, also dried-salted, commonly made into fish balls, and frozen, smoked or canned; a lipid-soluble ciguatoxin-like toxin has been found in the flesh of specimens from the east coast of Queensland, Australia.
records.source_quote: Marketed mainly fresh; also dried-salted; commonly made into fish balls (Ref. 9684), frozen, smoked, and canned (Ref. 9987). ... A lipid-soluble toxin, similar to ciguatoxin has been found in the flesh of specimens caught on the east coast of Queensland, Australia.

records.content: LIMITATION: the label 'gembolo' is unresolved; the FishBase common-name search for 'Gembolo' returns no matching entry, so no scientific identity can be assigned and identity or culinary claims require expert confirmation.
records.source_quote: List of Common Names for 'Gembolo' using Taxamatch[n=0] ... No results found.

records.content: Pressure-steamed milkfish had the hardest texture among the cooking methods tested; this describes the pressure-steamed product, not uncooked milkfish.
records.source_quote: Pressure steamed milkfish had the highest a* and b* values and produced the hardest texture.

records.content: Eleutheronema tetradactylum is marketed fresh, frozen, dried, or salted.
records.source_quote: Marketed fresh, frozen and dried or salted (Ref. 9987).

records.content: Johnius trachycephalus has 9-10 dorsal spines, 24-27 dorsal soft rays, two anal spines, and 6-7 anal soft rays.
records.source_quote: Dorsal spines (total): 9 - 10; Dorsal soft rays (total): 24-27; Anal spines: 2; Anal soft rays: 6 - 7.

records.content: Johnius trachycephalus has been studied as potential raw material for surimi and processed fish-meat products; this establishes investigated potential, not industrial adoption.
records.source_quote: Studi Potensi Ikan Gulamah (Johnius trachycephalus) Sebagai Bahan Baku Surimi dan Produk Olahan Berbasis Daging Ikan

records.content: Gelatin isolated from Johnius trachycephalus bones has been studied for jelly-candy application; this establishes an experimental use.
records.source_quote: Isolasi Gelatin dari Tulang Ikan Gulamah (Johnius trachycephalus) dan Aplikasinya Pada Permen Jelly

records.content: Sausage made from 100% Nibea albiflora received a reported texture score of 5.00 and taste score of 5.40; this describes the processed sausage.
records.source_quote: Sosis ikan gulamah 100% menghasilkan kenampakan (5,17%), aroma dan tekstur (5,00%), dan rasa (5,40%) dengan protein sebesar (6,67%)

records.content: Nibea albiflora was processed into a 100% fish sausage and a formulation with 30% chicken meat for sensory and proximate testing.
records.source_quote: Pada penelitian ini dilakukan 2 perlakuan yakni sosis ikan 100% dan sosis ikan dengan penambahan daging ayam 30% kemudian dilakukan uji mutu sensori menggunakan uji kesukaan skala 1-7 dan uji proksimat.

records.content: The Gascoyne-Lyons Oreochromis mossambicus population was reported as highly stunted, maturing at a mean standard length of 9 cm versus about 18 cm in other populations; this is population-specific.
records.source_quote: The available evidence suggests that the O. mossambicus population in the Gascoyne-Lyons system (24°S; 166°E) is highly stunted, reaching maturity at a mean standard length of 9 cm as opposed to populations from other locations which reach maturity around 18 cm (Blühdörn and Arthington, 1990).

records.content: Oreochromis mossambicus supports an important artisanal floodplain fishery in Papua New Guinea's Sepik River and accounts for about half of estimated annual landings.
records.source_quote: Oreochromis mossambicus supports an important floodplain, artisanal fishery in the Sepik River, and accounts for about 50 percent of the landings, estimated to be about 3 000 - 5 000 tonnes/year (Coates, 1987b).

records.content: Nile tilapia can be processed into skinless fillets; FAO reports a 33 percent skinless-fillet yield for fish with a condition factor of 3.11.
records.source_quote: Nile tilapia with a condition factor of 3.11 will dress at 86 percent with head, 66 percent without head, and 33 percent for a skinless fillet.

records.content: Pacific yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares), one species within Fishora's genus-level tuna label, is torpedo-shaped, metallic dark blue above, yellow-to-silver below, with bright yellow dorsal and anal fins and finlets.
records.source_quote: Yellowfin tuna are torpedo-shaped. They are metallic dark blue on the back and upper sides and change from yellow to silver on the belly. True to their name, their dorsal and anal fins and finlets are bright yellow.

records.content: Pacific yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares), one species within Fishora's genus-level tuna label, has a mild, meaty flavor and firm, moist meat with large flakes.
records.source_quote: Yellowfin tuna has a mild, meaty flavor. It’s more flavorful than albacore, but leaner than bluefin. The meat is firm and moist, with large flakes.

records.content: Albacore (Thunnus alalunga), one species within Fishora's genus-level tuna label, is marketed fresh, smoked, deep-frozen, or canned.
records.source_quote: Highly appreciated and marketed fresh, smoked, deep frozen or canned.

records.content: Yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares), one species within Fishora's genus-level tuna label, is marketed fresh, frozen, canned, and smoked, and is valued for sashimi.
records.source_quote: Marketed mainly fresh, frozen, canned (Ref. 9684), but also smoked (Ref. 9987). Highly valued for sashimi (Ref. 26938).

records.content: Scomberomorus commerson, one candidate species within the ambiguous tenggiri label, has 15-18 dorsal spines.
records.source_quote: Dorsal spines (total): 15 - 18

records.content: Scomberomorus commerson, one candidate species within the ambiguous tenggiri label, is marketed mainly fresh and also dried-salted, frozen, smoked, and canned.
records.source_quote: Marketed mainly fresh and also dried-salted, frozen, smoked and canned.

records.content: Island mackerel (Rastrelliger faughni) has a moderately deep body with the head longer than the body depth, very long gillrakers visible when the mouth is open, narrow dark longitudinal bands on the upper body (golden in fresh specimens), a black spot near the lower margin of the pectoral fin, and yellowish dorsal fins with black tips.
records.source_quote: Body moderately deep, its depth at margin of gill cover 4.3 to 5.2 times in fork length; head longer than body depth. ... gillrakers very long, visible when mouth is opened ... Colour: narrow dark longitudinal bands on upper part of body (golden in fresh specimens) and a black spot on body near lower margin of pectoral fin; dorsal fins yellowish with black tips, caudal and pectoral fins yellowish; other fins dusky.

records.content: The Indonesian name Kembung is also a local name of the Indian mackerel Rastrelliger kanagurta, a similar species of the same genus; island mackerel is caught along with the other Rastrelliger species, separate statistics are not reported for it, and some local names of the other two Rastrelliger species may apply to R. faughni.
records.source_quote: Separate statistics are not reported for Island mackerel, but it is taken along with other species of Rastrelliger off Taiwan Island, the Philippines, Indonesia, and Malaysia. ... Local Names : INDONESIA: Kembung ... some of the local names here given for the other two species of Rastrelliger and for Scomber australasicus may apply to R. faughni in some localities. ... Rastrelliger kanagurta ... INDONESIA: Banjar, Kembung, Kembunglelaki

records.content: Scomberomorus commerson (Spanish mackerel), one candidate species within the ambiguous tenggiri label, has a strong, distinctly fishy flavour, medium to very high oiliness, medium-dry firm flesh and few bones that are easily removed.
records.source_quote: Has a strong, distinctly 'fishy' flavour, medium to very high oiliness and medium-dry, firm flesh ... has few bones, which are easily removed.

records.content: In the Australian market, S. commerson (one candidate species within the tenggiri label) is sold mainly as cutlets and steaks, usually skinned; the average yield is 40%.
records.source_quote: Sold mainly as cutlets and steaks. ... Average yield is 40% ... The thin skin can be eaten, but it's usually sold skinned

records.content: Sydney Fish Market lists other mackerels, bonito, striped marlin, swordfish and tunas as alternatives to Spanish mackerel (S. commerson, one candidate species within the tenggiri label).
records.source_quote: Alternatives: Other Mackerels, Bonito, Striped Marlin, Swordfish, Tunas

records.content: Yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares), one species within Fishora's genus-level tuna label, has a medium flavour, medium oiliness and moist flesh that quickly becomes dry if overcooked; the cooked flesh is creamy brown, breaks into large flakes and has very few bones.
records.source_quote: Has a medium flavour, medium oiliness and moist flesh, which quickly becomes dry if overcooked. The cooked flesh is creamy brown in colour and breaks into large flakes; there are very few bones to worry about.

records.content: Yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares), one species within the tuna label, is usually sold as steaks, cutlets or sliced as sashimi, with an average yield of 70-75%; only sashimi-grade fish should be served raw or rare.
records.source_quote: Usually sold as steaks, cutlets or sliced as sashimi. ... Always buy sashimi-grade fish if it is to be served raw or rare. ... Average yield is 70-75%.

records.content: Sydney Fish Market lists Atlantic salmon, marlins, mackerels, swordfish, other tunas and yellowtail kingfish as alternatives to yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares, one species within the tuna label).
records.source_quote: Alternatives: Atlantic Salmon, Marlins, Mackerels, Swordfish, other Tunas, Yellowtail Kingfish

records.content: Eleutheronema tetradactylum is one of the most important fisheries species for Kuwait, India, Thailand, Viet Nam, Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia; it is mainly caught by gill net, sometimes by trawl, and is also an important sport fish in Australian waters.
records.source_quote: One of the most important fisheries species for Kuwait, India, Thailand, Viet Nam, Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia ... The species is mainly caught by gill net, sometimes by trawl ... The species is also an important sport fish in Australian waters

records.content: Eleutheronema tetradactylum is not known from East Asia, where it is replaced by the endemic congener Eleutheronema rhadinum, a similar threadfin species.
records.source_quote: The species is not known from East Asia (where it is replaced by the endemic E. rhadinum).

records.content: Milkfish flesh is bony; FAO notes that the younger generation tends to avoid eating milkfish because of their bony flesh.
records.source_quote: the younger generation tends to avoid eating milkfish because of their bony flesh

records.content: Farmed milkfish of 200-400 g are marketed mostly fresh or chilled, whole or deboned, frozen, or processed (fresh frozen deboned, deboned and descaled, smoked deboned); value-added forms include smoked, dried, marinated, rice-fermented, and canned or bottled milkfish, and some Philippine companies produce frozen prime cuts of bellies and backs.
records.source_quote: 200-400 g milkfish are harvested and marketed mostly fresh or chilled, whole or deboned, frozen, or processed (e.g. fresh frozen deboned, fresh frozen deboned descaled, and smoked fish deboned). ... Increasingly, more of the milkfish harvest is processed into value-added forms: smoked, dried, marinated (brined, sweetened), fermented with rice, and canned or bottled in various styles ... Some companies in the Philippines now produce frozen prime cuts of milkfish bellies and backs

records.content: Milkfish producers usually sell through cooperatives, brokers, dealers, collectors or wholesalers rather than directly to consumers, mostly via auction markets; milkfish is exported quick-frozen, dried, canned, smoked or marinated, and Indonesia's milkfish market includes seed production exports.
records.source_quote: Producers of milkfish do not usually sell fish directly to consumers, but supply them through cooperatives, brokers, dealers, collectors or wholesalers, and retailers. In general, the majority of fish products are sold in auction markets ... Milkfish is exported in different product forms: quick-frozen, dried, canned, smoked or marinated. ... Indonesia with its seed production exports

records.content: Farmed tilapia can have an off-flavour: in developed countries a fillet is cooked unseasoned and tasted before processing, and off-flavour fish are purged in clean water for 3-7 days; in developing countries spicy seasonings in cooking conceal any off-flavour.
records.source_quote: Tilapia must be tested for flavour before they will be accepted for processing and marketing in developed countries. ... If they are off-flavour, they are purged in clean water for 3-7 days in holding tanks or ponds. This procedure is generally not practised in developing countries where the use of spicy seasonings in the cooking process conceals any off-flavour.

records.content: Tilapia are hauled live to processing plants, killed in ice water and processed manually or mechanically; fillets are sold fresh or frozen as skin-on, skin-off, deep skinned, individually quick frozen, smoked and sashimi grade, and whole or gutted tilapia are still available.
records.source_quote: Tilapia are hauled live to processing plants, killed humanely in ice water and processed manually or mechanically. ... Today, fresh or frozen fillets are available in different sizes and packages, as skin-on, skin-off, deep skinned, individually quick frozen, smoked, and sashimi grade ... Whole or gutted tilapia are still available

records.content: Several tilapia species are cultured commercially, with Nile tilapia the predominant one; FAO describes tilapia as ideally suited to replace carp as the staple of Chinese seafood.
records.source_quote: Several species of tilapia are cultured commercially, but Nile tilapia is the predominant cultured species worldwide. ... Tilapia is ideally suited to replace carp as the staple of Chinese seafood.

records.content: Oreochromis mossambicus was the tilapia primarily distributed worldwide in the 1940s and 1950s; the Nile tilapia (O. niloticus), described by FAO as more desirable, was distributed from the 1960s to the 1980s.
records.source_quote: While significant worldwide distribution of tilapias, primarily Oreochromis mossambicus, occurred during the 1940s and 1950s, distribution of the more desirable Nile tilapia occurred during the 1960s up to the 1980s.

records.content: Kembung (Rastrelliger spp.), the fish known as gembolo or gambolo in West Sumatra, has a dark blue-green to brownish back with one or two rows of dark spots near the dorsal fin base and silvery ventral scales.
records.source_quote: Sisi dorsal gelap, biru kehijauan hingga kecoklatan, dengan 1–2 deret bintik gelap membujur di dekat pangkal sirip punggung; sisik ventral keperakan.

records.content: Rastrelliger mackerels, the genus sold as gembolo in West Sumatra, have a blue-green back with two rows of small dark spots along the dorsal fin bases.
records.source_quote: Colour: back blue-green with 2 rows of small, dark spots on sides of dorsal fin bases

records.content: Rastrelliger brachysoma (short mackerel), one of the Rastrelliger fishes sold as gembolo, reaches a maximum fork length of 34.5 cm and is commonly 15 to 20 cm.
records.source_quote: Maximum fork length is 34.5 cm, common from 15 to 20 cm

records.content: Rastrelliger kanagurta, one of the Rastrelliger mackerels sold as gembolo in West Sumatra, was chosen for a fish snack study because it tastes good and is cheap.
records.source_quote: it taste good and tasty, and the price are cheap

records.content: Rastrelliger mackerels, the genus sold as gembolo in West Sumatra, are marketed fresh, frozen, canned, dried-salted and smoked.
records.source_quote: The fish are marketed fresh, frozen, canned, dried salted and smoked.

records.content: Gambolo (Rastrelliger spp.) is usually sold fresh or processed into preserved products including salted fish (ikan asin).
records.source_quote: biasonyo dijuwa baru atau diproses manjadi ikan tangguang jo ikan asin

records.content: Rastrelliger brachysoma (short mackerel), one of the fishes sold as gembolo, is typically fried in Thailand and eaten with nam phrik kapi.
records.source_quote: is typically fried and eaten with

records.content: Kembung (Rastrelliger spp.), known as gembolo in West Sumatra, is a small pelagic fish of medium economic value and an important commodity for local fishers.
records.source_quote: Kembung termasuk ikan pelagis kecil yang memiliki nilai ekonomis menengah, sehingga terhitung sebagai komoditas yang cukup penting bagi nelayan lokal.

records.content: Small kembung (Rastrelliger spp., called gembolo in West Sumatra) are often used as live bait for skipjack tuna fishing.
records.source_quote: Ikan kembung yang masih kecil juga sering digunakan sebagai umpan hidup untuk memancing cakalang.

records.content: Rastrelliger brachysoma (short mackerel), one of the fishes sold as gembolo, is a highly commercial fisheries species and also a gamefish.
records.source_quote: Fisheries: highly commercial; gamefish: yes

records.content: The Thai market name for Rastrelliger brachysoma (one of the fishes sold as gembolo) is sometimes also applied to Indian mackerel (Rastrelliger kanagurta), which is prepared the same way.
records.source_quote: is sometimes also applied to the

records.content: Some common names for Rastrelliger brachysoma, one of the fishes sold as gembolo, may also or exclusively refer to island mackerel (Rastrelliger faughni).
records.source_quote: Some common names listed for this species may also or exclusively be in use for R. faughni.

records.content: Indian mackerel (Rastrelliger kanagurta, kembung) was chosen for a fish snack study because it is nutritious, tastes good and is cheap.
records.source_quote: Mackerel (Rastrelliger kanagurta) was chosen because it has a good nutrient for the body, one of them protein and calcium, it taste good and tasty, and the price are cheap.

records.content: In snack sticks made from kembung (Rastrelliger kanagurta), the stick made from the fish meat was preferred for texture.
records.source_quote: Fish meat stick favored in texture

records.content: Kembung (Rastrelliger spp.) is usually sold fresh or processed into longer-lasting pindang (boiled-salted) fish and salted fish (ikan asin).
records.source_quote: Kembung biasanya dijual segar atau diproses menjadi ikan pindang dan ikan asin yang lebih tahan lama.

records.content: Rastrelliger kanagurta (Indian mackerel, kembung) is generally marketed fresh, frozen, canned, dried-salted and smoked, and is also made into fish sauce.
records.source_quote: Generally marketed fresh, frozen, canned, dried-salted, and smoked; also made into fish sauce

records.content: Island mackerel (Rastrelliger faughni) is reported together with the other Rastrelliger species (Indian and short mackerel) in landings statistics.
records.source_quote: in the landings statistics, it is reported together with the other

records.content: A 2022 study from West Kalimantan reports that the flesh of the leaftail croaker (gulamah, Johnius trachycephalus) is relatively thick, which gives a high meat yield and makes it a strong candidate raw material for surimi.
records.source_quote: Daging ikan gulamah relatif lebih tebal sehingga sangat potensial digunakan sebagai bahan baku surimi karena menghasilkan rendemen yang tinggi.

records.content: Surimi gel made from gulamah (Johnius trachycephalus) flesh measured a gel strength of 932.55 g/cm2 in Texture Profile Analyzer testing.
records.source_quote: Karakeristik gel surimi berdasarkan uji Tekstur Profile Analyzer didapatkan nilai kekuatan gel (Gel strength) sebesar 932,55 g/cm2

records.content: Croakers of the genera Pennahia and Johnius are among the marine fish most often used as surimi raw material in the surimi industry, alongside threadfin bream, bigeye snapper, lizardfish and goatfish.
records.source_quote: Jenis ikan laut sebagai bahan baku surimi yang paling sering digunakan pada industri surimi adalah ikan threadfin bream (Nemipterus spp.), bigeye snapper (Priacanthus spp.), croakers (Pennahia and Johnius spp.), lizardfish (Saurida spp.), dan goat fish/red mullet (Upeneus spp, Parupeneus spp.).

records.content: The FAO identification sheet for the leaftail croaker (Johnius trachycephalus) lists similar croakers in the same area, including Johnius dussumieri, J. coitor, J. belangerii, J. carutta and J. hypostomus; J. dussumieri can be told apart by the barbel on its chin.
records.source_quote: DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERS OF SIMILAR SPECIES OCCURRING IN THE AREA: Johnius dussumieri: barbel present on chin.

records.content: FishBase gives a maximum length of 43.5 cm standard length for the yellow drum (Nibea albiflora).
records.source_quote: Max length : 43.5 cm SL male/unsexed

records.content: The yellow drum (Nibea albiflora) can grow to about 44 cm in length and about 1.5 kg in weight.
records.source_quote: The yellow drum can grow to ~44 cm in length and ~1.5 kg in weight

records.content: The yellow drum (Nibea albiflora) shares similar external characteristics, meat quality and flavour with the large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea).
records.source_quote: Yellow drum shares similar external characteristics, meat quality and flavors with large yellow croaker.

records.content: The yellow drum is expected to partly replace the large yellow croaker in the market, because large yellow croaker supply suffers from overfishing and disease in aquaculture.
records.source_quote: Now, yellow drum is expected to partially replace the market of the large yellow croaker, which suffers from the shortage of germplasm resource due to overfishing and severe bacterial and virus diseases in aquaculture

records.content: In Chinese fish markets, the yellow drum sells at a price similar to that of the large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea).
records.source_quote: The market price of the yellow drum is similar to that of the large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea), which is another popular fish sold in local Chinese fish markets.

records.content: FAO describes the flesh of goatfishes (family Mullidae, which includes Upeneus moluccensis) as of good quality, with some species highly esteemed in certain countries.
records.source_quote: The flesh of goatfishes is of good quality and that of some species highly esteemed in certain countries.

records.content: The yellowfin goatfish (Mulloidichthys vanicolensis) is often confused with the goldband goatfish (Upeneus moluccensis) because it also has a single golden band along its sides.
records.source_quote: Mulloidichthys vanicolensis: often confused with U. moluccensis because it also has a single golden band along sides

records.content: Threadfin salmons such as the blue (fourfinger) threadfin have firm flesh with large flakes that suits barbecuing or grilling as steaks, cutlets or fillets.
records.source_quote: Their firm flesh and large flakes make them absolutely ideal for barbecuing or grilling in steaks, cutlets or fillets, depending on size and variety.

records.content: Threadfin salmons, including the blue threadfin, are good-eating tropical fish that readily absorb the flavours of other ingredients.
records.source_quote: Threadfin salmons are good eating tropical finfish that readily absorb the flavours of other ingredients.

records.content: The Western Australian fisheries fact sheet says the blue threadfin (Eleutheronema tetradactylum) is considered excellent eating.
records.source_quote: Considered to be excellent eating.

records.content: The East Asian fourfinger threadfin (Eleutheronema rhadinum) was historically misidentified as the fourfinger threadfin (E. tetradactylum) because the two look very similar.
records.source_quote: was historically misidentified as E. tetradactylum due to their high degree of morphological similarity

records.content: In Australia the fourfinger threadfin (Eleutheronema tetradactylum) goes by local names that call it a salmon, such as blue salmon, Cooktown salmon and Rockhampton salmon.
records.source_quote: Local Names: AUSTRALIA: Blue threadfin, Blue salmon, Cooktown salmon, Rockhampton salmon, Giant threadfin,

records.content: Narrow-barred Spanish mackerel has a strong, distinctly fishy flavour, medium to very high oiliness and medium-dry, firm flesh.
records.source_quote: Has a strong, distinctly 'fishy' flavour, medium to very high oiliness and medium-dry, firm flesh.

records.content: Spanish mackerel has a thin edible skin but is usually sold skinned, and it has few bones, which are easily removed.
records.source_quote: The thin skin can be eaten, but it's usually sold skinned and has few bones, which are easily removed.

records.content: Good-quality Spanish mackerel cutlets and steaks have bright off-white, firm, lustrous, moist flesh without dark brown markings or oozing water.
records.source_quote: In cutlets and steaks look for bright off-white, firm, lustrous, moist flesh without any dark brown markings or oozing water and with a pleasant fresh sea smell.

records.content: Sydney Fish Market lists other mackerels, bonito, striped marlin, swordfish and tunas as alternative species for Spanish mackerel.
records.source_quote: Other Mackerels, Bonito, Striped Marlin, Swordfish, Tunas

records.content: Spanish mackerel looks similar to grey mackerel, especially when young, because of the dark vertical bars along its sides.
records.source_quote: It looks similar to Grey Mackerel, especially when young, due to the dark vertical bars along the sides.

records.content: Before it was formally described, the Queensland school mackerel (Scomberomorus queenslandicus) was confused with the spotted Spanish mackerel S. guttatus.
records.source_quote: Prior to its description, this species was confused with S. guttatus.

records.content: In Japan, bigeye tuna (Thunnus obesus) meat is highly priced and processed into sashimi as a substitute for bluefin tuna.
records.source_quote: In Japan, its meat is highly priced and processed into sashimi in substitution for bluefin tuna.

records.content: The name 'albacore', normally used for Thunnus alalunga, is used by French speakers in the eastern Atlantic for yellowfin tuna (T. albacares).
records.source_quote: while in the eastern Atlantic "albacore" is used by francophones for the yellowfin tuna (T. albacares).

records.content: Sydney Fish Market lists Atlantic salmon, marlins, mackerels, swordfish, other tunas and yellowtail kingfish as alternative species for yellowfin tuna.
records.source_quote: Atlantic Salmon, Marlins, Mackerels, Swordfish, other Tunas, Yellowtail Kingfish

records.content: Milkfish (Chanos chanos) is reported, together with tilapia, common carp and mud carp, among the less expensive fish used to replace costly fish.
records.source_quote: Replacement of costly fish with some less expensive ones, such as tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), common carp (Cyprinus carpio), milkfish (Chanos chanos), and mud cap (Cirrhinus molitorella), is reported.

records.content: In Taiwanese fish surimi products, milkfish was one of the main fish species identified, alongside dolphinfish, pomfret, swordfish and cartilaginous fishes.
records.source_quote: The main fish species identified included milkfish (Chanos chanos), dolphinfish (Coryphaena hippurus), Pomfret (Taractes rubescens), swordfish (Istiophorus spp.) and cartilaginous.

records.content: Oreochromis mossambicus introduced to Nauru became a pest rather than a food fish, partly because of its unattractive appearance compared to milkfish.
records.source_quote: Rather than becoming a food fish, it became a pest for reasons of its unattractive appearance compared to milkfish, small size and mainly because of its effect on milkfish farming.

records.content: The Taiwanese strain of red hybrid tilapia was produced by crossing mutant reddish-orange female Oreochromis mossambicus with normal male O. niloticus.
records.source_quote: Mutant reddish-orange female Oreochromis mossambicus (Peters, 1852) and normal male O. niloticus crosses have been used to produce the Taiwanese strain

records.content: Red hybrid tilapia is valued partly because its colour resembles premium marine species such as sea bream (Pagrus major) and red snapper (Lutjanus argentimaculatus).
records.source_quote: Due to its characteristic colour resemblance to premium marine species such as the sea bream (Pagrus major (Temminck & Schlegel, 1843)) and red snapper (Lutjanus argentimaculatus

records.content: In a Taiwan market study, all 11 products sold as snapper that were substituted were confirmed by DNA to be Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus).
records.source_quote: The substituted snappers are the largest mislabel category, where all 11 substituted snappers are molecularly confirmed to be tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus, Table 1).

records.content: In Taiwan, substitution of snapper by tilapia stems from the practice of labelling tilapia as 'Taiwan-Snapper'.
records.source_quote: The substitution of snapper by tilapia is actually originated from the confusing practice of labeling Tilapia as Taiwan-Snapper

records.content: FAO states that tilapia is ideally suited to replace carp as the staple of Chinese seafood.
records.source_quote: Tilapia is ideally suited to replace carp as the staple of Chinese seafood.
